<result>Teams are defined in migration 010 (latest migration is 068). There are two main reasons users see people outside their own team:
- **`GET /api/team/members`** lists whichever team the user happens to be matched to. That match is not deterministic, so it can be a big shared team rather than the user's own.
- **The project-settings "add member" picker** lists every user in any team you share, not just the project's team.

On top of that, user search covers every registered user, and any user can add anyone to their team without that person agreeing.

## 1. DB schema

Migrations live in two parallel folders: SQLite in `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/internal/db/migrations/*.sql` and Postgres in `.../migrations/postgres/*.sql`. Tests run on SQLite, loaded from `./../../internal/db/migrations` (`api/internal/api/testing.go:44`).

**Latest migration: `068_wiki_page_hierarchy.sql` in both folders, so the next one is 069.** The numbering drifts between the two:
- SQLite has no 066; its 064 is milestones and 065 is tasks_updated_by.
- Postgres 064 is wiki_vector_embeddings, 065 is milestones, 066 is tasks_updated_by.

The migrations that matter here:

| Migration | What it does |
|---|---|
| `005_add_project_sharing_and_github.sql` | Original `project_members` (id, project_id, user_id, role viewer/editor/admin, added_by, created_at, UNIQUE(project_id,user_id)). Original `project_invitations` (email-based). |
| `010_add_teams.sql` | Creates `teams`, `team_members`, `team_invitations`. Adds `team_id` to `projects`, `sprints` and `tags`. Backfills one team per user named "`<email>'s Team`", adds the user as owner, and assigns their projects, sprints and tags to it. |
| `011_add_project_members.sql` | `project_members` (id, project_id, user_id, role default 'member' [owner/editor/member/viewer], granted_by, granted_at, UNIQUE(project_id,user_id)). |
| `012_backfill_team_project_access.sql` | Rebuilds `project_members` (SQLite) and auto-grants every active team member access to all of their team's projects. |
| `020_add_team_invite_token.sql` | Adds `team_invitations.acceptance_token` (unique index), `token_expires_at`, `invite_code`. |
| `031_explicit_project_access.sql` | `DELETE FROM project_members WHERE role != 'owner'`. This undoes the 012 backfill: from here on, project access is explicit only. |
| `032_project_invitations.sql` | Drops and recreates `project_invitations`: id, project_id, inviter_id, invitee_user_id, role default 'member', status default 'pending', invited_at, responded_at, last_sent_at, UNIQUE(project_id, invitee_user_id). Invitations now target a user id, not an email. |

The team tables (from 010):
- **`teams`**: id, name, owner_id → users, created_at, updated_at. Only `owner_id` is indexed; it is not unique.
- **`team_members`**: id, team_id, user_id, role ('owner'/'admin'/'member'), status ('active'/'inactive'), joined_at, UNIQUE(team_id,user_id). **Nothing stops a user belonging to several teams.**
- **`team_invitations`**: id, team_id, inviter_id, invitee_email, invitee_id (nullable until the user signs up), status (pending/accepted/rejected/cancelled), created_at, responded_at, plus the three columns from 020.
- **`projects.team_id`** is nullable and references teams with ON DELETE CASCADE.

The ent schemas are in `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/ent/schema/{team,teammember,teaminvitation}.go`.

## 2. Team endpoints

Routes are in `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/cmd/api/main.go:608-625`, all behind JWTAuth. The public token lookup is at `:429`. Handlers are in `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/internal/api/team_handlers.go`, and most use ent rather than raw SQL.

**How the "current team" is chosen**
- `getUserTeamID` (`team_handlers.go:985-996`) runs `TeamMember.Query().Where(user_id=X, status='active').First(ctx)`. **There is no ORDER BY**, so a user in more than one team gets whichever row the database returns first. There is no stored "current team" and no team switcher.
- `getUserTeamRole` (`:998-1010`) returns the user's role in that team.
- Every user gets their own team as owner at signup: `auth_handlers.go:143-170` for password signup, `internal/db/oauth_store.go:157-178` for OAuth. So everyone owns one team and can join more.
- Accepting a team invite adds a second `team_members` row. From then on, "my team" can resolve to either team.

The handlers:

| Endpoint | Handler | Query | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/team` | `HandleGetMyTeam` :87 | `Team.Query().Where(HasMembersWith(user_id, active)).First()`, also unordered | Any member |
| GET `/api/team/members` | `HandleGetTeamMembers` :122 | All `team_members` of `getUserTeamID`'s team, with user, ordered role DESC, joined_at ASC. No status filter, so inactive members show too. | **None beyond "has an active membership"** |
| POST `/api/team/invite` | `HandleInviteTeamMember` :170 | Checks for an existing member or pending invite. If the email is already registered, it **auto-accepts**: writes an invitation with status 'accepted' and a `team_members` row in one transaction (:258-335). Otherwise it creates a pending invitation, token and invite code, and sends an email. | Team role owner or admin |
| POST `/api/team/members` | `HandleAddTeamMember` :885 | Adds any `user_id` straight into `team_members`. **The added user is never asked.** | Owner or admin |
| DELETE `/api/team/members/{memberId}` | `HandleRemoveTeamMember` :606 | Deletes the row, scoped to the caller's team. The owner can't be removed. | Owner or admin |
| GET `/api/team/users/search?q=` | `HandleSearchUsers` :825 | Searches **all users** by email, name, first_name or last_name (case-insensitive contains), excluding current team members, LIMIT 10 | Owner or admin, which **every user is, of their own team** |
| GET `/api/team/memberships` | `HandleGetMyTeamMemberships` :746 | The user's active memberships in teams they don't own | Self |
| GET `/api/team/invitations` | `HandleGetMyInvitations` :406 | Pending invitations where invitee_id or invitee_email matches the caller | Self |
| GET `/api/team/invitations/sent` | `HandleGetTeamSentInvitations` :784 | Pending invitations for the caller's current team | **Any member**, no role check |
| POST `/api/team/invitations/{id}/accept` and `/reject` | :459, :547 | Updates the invitation and inserts a `team_members` row (role member) | Invitee's email or id must match |
| GET `/api/team/invitations/by-token` (public), POST `/accept-by-token` | :1060, :1122 | Token lookup; accept requires the email to match | Public / authenticated |
| PATCH `/api/team` | `HandleUpdateTeam` :675 | Renames the team | Owner or admin |
| GET `/api/me/collaborators` | `HandleGetCollaborators` :1254-1313 | Raw SQL: every user other than the caller who shares **any** active team with them (a self-join on `team_members`), ordered by email | Self |

**Why a user sees everyone:**
- In Settings, `GET /team/members` shows the roster of the team `getUserTeamID` picks. If the user has joined a big shared team (say an org owner invited everybody), the unordered `First()` can return that team, and they see its whole roster.
- In the project picker, `/me/collaborators` returns the union of every team the user belongs to. One all-hands team makes every user a collaborator of every other user.
- Team search is global, and add-member doesn't ask the other person. So any user can pull anyone into their team, and after that the shared-team check that guards project invites passes.

Other team code paths:
- `auth_handlers.go:500-551` (`acceptPendingTeamInvitation` at signup) and `oauth_store.go:225-280`.
- Admin force-accept: `admin_handlers.go:807`, route `/admin/team-invitations/{id}/resolve`.

## 3. Projects and teams, and the "add member" flow

**Creating a project** (`project_handlers.go:111-170`): sets `team_id = getUserTeamID(...)`, which inherits the nondeterminism, and inserts the creator into `project_members` as 'owner'.

**How much `team_id` is used:** very little. Project access goes entirely through `project_members`:
- `userHasProjectAccess` at `project_settings_handlers.go:543`
- `checkProjectAccess` at `task_handlers.go:1505`

The only place that reads `projects.team_id` is GitHub user auto-matching, `github_handlers.go:945-951`.

The project-member handlers are in `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/internal/api/project_settings_handlers.go`, with routes at `main.go:566-590`:
- **GET `/projects/{id}/members`** (:71): project members joined to users. Requires project access.
- **POST `/projects/{id}/members`** (:126): the legacy direct add by email. Requires project owner or admin, and that the two users share an active team (:189-208). Then inserts into `project_members`.
- **POST `/projects/{id}/invitations`** (:617): the flow the UI uses. It:
  - requires project owner or admin (:630),
  - rejects the project owner as invitee,
  - applies the same shared-team EXISTS check (:676-694),
  - rejects existing members,
  - upserts `project_invitations` with ON CONFLICT → pending (:711),
  - sends an email and a websocket `project_invitation` event.
- **Accepting** (`/project-invitations/{id}/accept`, :822): the invitee id must match. In one transaction it sets status accepted and inserts into `project_members` (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), then broadcasts `project_membership`.
- Also: reject :908, withdraw :953, resend (48h cooldown) :999, `/my/project-invitations` :1080, count :1132.

One quirk: `userIsProjectOwnerOrAdmin` (:568-590) checks `role == "admin"`. The valid project roles are viewer, member, editor and owner, so a project member with role 'owner' who isn't `projects.owner_id` is not treated as an admin.

**Which users the "add member" picker shows:** `ProjectSettings.tsx:185-190` calls `getCollaborators()`, i.e. `/api/me/collaborators`, which covers every team you share. It filters out existing members and pending invitees at :554-557 and renders a `SearchSelect` at :700-738. So yes, it lists members of all your teams, not just the project's team. This comes from commit a2a0325 ("fix: allow cross-team project member invites").

## 4. Other places that expose users

- **Team search** (`HandleSearchUsers`): the widest exposure. Any user can look up every registered user by email or name substring.
- **Admin**: `GET /admin/users` (`admin_handlers.go:49`, guarded by `isAdmin` at :345). `/admin/invitations` (:641-686) joins team and project invitations with users. Admin analytics users: `admin_analytics_handlers.go:202, 298`. All admin-only.
- **User profile**: `/users/{id}/profile` and `/users/{id}/activity` (`user_profile_handlers.go:50-110`) require a shared project via a self-join on `project_members`. Properly scoped.
- **@mentions**: the frontend `MentionTextarea.tsx:29` uses `getProjectMembers`. The backend mention resolution (`notification_handlers.go:224`) is also limited to `project_members`.
- **Assignee picker**: `TaskDetail.tsx:381-383, 1318-1330` uses `getProjectMembers`. **But the backend doesn't check that `assignee_ids` are project members** (`task_handlers.go:654-659` on create, `replaceTaskAssignees` at :1492 on update), so any user id is accepted.
- **GitHub discover-mappings** (`github_handlers.go:945`): matches against all members of the project's team.
- **Legacy add-by-email** (`project_settings_handlers.go:164`): looks up any user by email, though the shared-team check follows.

## 5. Frontend

API client, `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/lib/api.ts`:
- Team functions (:1567-1645): `getMyTeam`, `getTeamMembers`, `getCollaborators`, `inviteTeamMember`, `removeTeamMember`, `getMyInvitations`, `getMyTeamMemberships`, `acceptInvitation`/`rejectInvitation`, `getInvitationByToken`/`acceptInvitationByToken`, `updateTeam`, `getTeamSentInvitations`, `searchTeamUsers`, `addTeamMember`.
- Project functions (:1099-1156): members, invitations, and `/my/project-invitations`.
- Admin functions: around :1306-1360.
- Types (:506-560): `Team`, `TeamMember`, `Collaborator`, `TeamInvitation`, `TeamMembership`.

Pages and components:
- **`web/src/routes/Settings.tsx`** (team tab): `loadTeamData` (:598-618) calls getMyTeam, getTeamMembers, getMyInvitations, getTeamSentInvitations and getMyTeamMemberships together. It includes:
  - rename (:680),
  - search-then-add-or-invite (:703, :730, :749),
  - the member list (:2212-2260),
  - "Teams you've joined" (:2305).
- **`web/src/routes/ProjectSettings.tsx`**: members and collaborators picker as described in section 3 (:160-190, :505-557, :700-745).
- **`web/src/routes/AcceptTeamInvite.tsx`**: token acceptance.
- **`web/src/components/ProjectInvitationBanner.tsx`** and **`web/src/state/NotificationContext.tsx:128`**: project invitation accept/reject.
- **`web/src/routes/Admin.tsx`**: admin users and invitations.
- **`web/src/routes/TaskDetail.tsx`** and **`web/src/components/MentionTextarea.tsx`**: pickers built from project members.

**Go, `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/internal/api/team_handlers_test.go`** (about 50 tests):
- Helpers: `createTestTeam` :13, `addTeamMember` :45, `createTestTeamInvitation` :68, `createTestTeamInvitationWithToken` :93.

- **Not covered:** `HandleSearchUsers`, `HandleGetCollaborators`, `HandleGetMyTeamMemberships`, and the multi-team behaviour of `getUserTeamID`.

- Tests for get/add/update/remove member (:103, :228, :559, :788) and for `userHasProjectAccess` / `userIsProjectOwnerOrAdmin` (:1341, :1433).

- `ts := NewTestServer(t); defer ts.Close()` gives an in-memory SQLite database with migrations applied (`testing.go:31`).
- `ts.CreateTestUser` (:74) inserts only the user row and does **not** create a team, so tests build teams with raw SQL using `?` placeholders.

input.content:
# Plan: Real multi-team separation in TaskAI

## Context
Nakul, who is from Intelliviz, can see all of the Elastio team's members. The cause is that TaskAI effectively gives each user one team.

- **What happens today:**
  - The Elastio staff, Nakul and Faiz all ended up in Anshuman's one team.
  - `getUserTeamID` (`api/internal/api/team_handlers.go:985`) picks a team with an unordered `First()`, so a user's "current team" is random.
  - The UI can only manage that one team.
  - `/api/me/collaborators`, which feeds the project "add member" picker, returns every member of every team you share. That is how Nakul sees everyone.
  - `/api/team/users/search` searches **every registered user** in the system.
- **What we want:**
  - A user can belong to several teams, for example Elastio and Intelliviz.
  - Members of one team never see members of another.
  - Teams are easy to create, switch between and manage, including moving a person from one team to another.
  - Project access keeps working as it does now: an invite from Project Settings that the person accepts.

**Decisions from the user:**
- The project picker shows members **grouped by team**.
- Adding someone to a team **stays direct**. Nobody has to accept a team add.
- **I split the production data** after deploying: create Intelliviz, move Nakul and Faiz into it, and take them out of the Elastio team. I'll confirm the project list first.

## Backend (Go, `api/internal/api/`)

### 1. Team-scoped API in a new file, `teams_handlers.go`
Every route checks that the caller is an active member of `{teamId}`, and mutations also need the owner or admin role. The existing `getUserTeamRole` does this check.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/teams` | The caller's teams with `{id, name, role, member_count, is_owner}` |
| `POST /api/teams` | Creates a team `{name}`. The caller becomes owner. Runs in a transaction. |
| `PATCH /api/teams/{teamId}` | Renames the team |
| `DELETE /api/teams/{teamId}` | Owner only. Blocked while the team still has projects or is the owner's only team. |
| `GET /api/teams/{teamId}/members` | Active members only |
| `POST /api/teams/{teamId}/members` | Adds `{user_id}` or `{email}`. An existing user is added directly. An unknown email gets the existing invite flow. |
| `DELETE /api/teams/{teamId}/members/{memberId}` | Removes a member |
| `POST /api/teams/{teamId}/members/{memberId}/move` | Moves a member to `{target_team_id}` in one transaction. The caller must be owner or admin of both teams. |
| `GET /api/teams/{teamId}/invitations/sent` | Sent invitations |
| `DELETE /api/teams/{teamId}/leave` | The caller leaves the team. An owner can't leave their own team. |

- The existing member-add and invite logic moves into helpers that take `teamID`, so the old `/api/team/*` routes and the new routes share one code path.
- The legacy `/api/team*` routes keep working by resolving the team through the deterministic `getUserTeamID`.

### 2. Make `getUserTeamID` deterministic
Prefer a team the user owns, then fall back to the earliest `joined_at` or `id`. That matches the "home team".

### 3. Stop the global user search
`HandleSearchUsers` currently returns any user whose email or name contains the query. After the change it returns only:
- (a) members of the caller's other teams, which makes pulling someone in from a team you already share easy, or
- (b) an **exact** email match.

No more substring lookup across all users. The email-invite path still covers people nobody in the team knows yet.

### 4. Group collaborators by team
`HandleGetCollaborators` returns `team_id` and `team_name` with each row. The query joins `teams` and emits one row per (team, user), so a person in two teams appears under both. The project invite check that requires a shared team stays as it is.

### 5. Choose a project's team
- `CreateProjectRequest` takes an optional `team_id`. The caller must be an active member of it, otherwise the request gets 403. Without it, the project goes in the deterministic home team.
- `PATCH /api/projects/{id}` accepts `team_id`. Only the project owner can change it, and they must be a member of the target team.
- Project responses include `team_id` and `team_name`, if the struct doesn't already.

### 6. Register the routes in `api/cmd/api/main.go`
Add the new `/teams` routes next to the existing team routes (around line 607).

No schema migration is needed. The tables already support a user belonging to many teams.

## Frontend (`web/src/`)

### `lib/api.ts`
- Add `Team` list types.
- Add `listTeams`, `createTeam`, `renameTeam(teamId)`, `deleteTeam`, `getTeamMembersById`, `addTeamMemberTo(teamId, …)`, `removeTeamMemberFrom`, `moveTeamMember`, `leaveTeam`.
- Add `team_id` and `team_name` to `Collaborator` and `Project`.

### `routes/Settings.tsx`, Team tab
- A team switcher at the top: a list or selector of the user's teams showing role and member count, plus a **"+ New team"** button.

  - The UI can only manage that one team.
  - `/api/me/collaborators`, which feeds the project "add member" picker, returns every member of every team you share. That is how Nakul sees everyone.
  - `/api/team/users/search` searches **every registered user** in the system.
- **What we want:**
  - A user can belong to several teams, for example Elastio and Intelliviz.
  - Members of one team never see members of another.
  - Teams are easy to create, switch between and manage, including moving a person from one team to another.
  - Project access keeps working as it does now: an invite from Project Settings that the person accepts.

- The project picker shows members **grouped by team**.

Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

67				// revealing which team IDs exist.
68				respondError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "team not found", "not_found")
69				return 0, false
70			}
71			return teamID, true
72		}

74		teamID, err := s.getUserTeamID(ctx, userID)

55	// /teams/{teamId} use that team and require the caller to be an active member
56	// of it; the legacy /team routes fall back to the caller's home team. On
57	// failure the error response has already been written.
58	func (s *Server) resolveTeamID(ctx context.Context, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, userID int64) (int64, bool) {
59		if raw := chi.URLParam(r, "teamId"); raw != "" {
60			teamID, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
61			if err != nil || teamID <= 0 {
62				respondError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid team ID", "invalid_input")
63				return 0, false
64			}
65			if _, err := s.getUserTeamRole(ctx, userID, teamID); err != nil {
66				// Not distinguishing "doesn't exist" from "not a member" avoids
67				// revealing which team IDs exist.
68				respondError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "team not found", "not_found")
69				return 0, false
70			}
71			return teamID, true
72		}

74		teamID, err := s.getUserTeamID(ctx, userID)
75		if err != nil {

83	func (s *Server) HandleListMyTeams(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
84		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 5*time.Second)
85		defer cancel()
86	
87		userID := r.Context().Value(UserIDKey).(int64)

91	
92		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
93			SELECT t.id, t.name, t.owner_id, tm.role,
94			       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_members m WHERE m.team_id = t.id AND m.status = 'active'),
95			       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects p WHERE p.team_id = t.id)
96			FROM team_members tm
97			JOIN teams t ON t.id = tm.team_id
98			WHERE tm.user_id = $1 AND tm.status = 'active'
99			ORDER BY LOWER(t.name), t.id
100		`, userID)

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/anshumanbiswas/.claude/skills/dev-server

# Local Development Server

Start a local dev environment for any project that has a `.me.sh` adapter file.
All projects live under `~/play/` and use the unified runner at `~/play/me/scripts/server`.

## How It Works

Each project has:
- `.me.sh` — project adapter with metadata (name, ports, stack, DB type)
- `docker-compose.yml` — containerized services (postgres, redis, etc.)
- `script/server` or `scripts/server` — project-specific server management

## Steps

### 1. Detect the current project

Look for `.me.sh` in the current working directory to get project metadata:

```bash
source .me.sh  # Gets PROJECT_NAME, PROJECT_PORT_BACKEND, PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND, PROJECT_DB, PROJECT_DOMAIN, etc.
```

### 2. Parse the user's request

The user may specify:
- **Environment to point frontend at**: `prod`, `staging`, `uat`, or `local` (default: `local`)
- **What to start**: `all` (default), `frontend`, `backend`, `docker`

### 3. Start Docker services (database)

Most projects need PostgreSQL (or SQLite). Start the database via docker-compose:

```bash
cd <project_dir>
docker compose up -d postgres  # Start just postgres (not all services)
```

Wait for postgres to be healthy before proceeding:

```bash
docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U <user> -d <db>
```

If the project uses Redis too, also start it:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres redis
```

### 4. Start the backend (API server)

**Only needed when pointing to `local`.** When pointing to prod/staging/uat, skip this step — the Vite proxy forwards to the remote API directly.

Run the backend natively for hot-reload. Each project's `.me.sh` defines how:

```bash
# For projects with Makefile:
cd <project_dir>/api && make dev

# Or use the adapter's local_dev function via the universal runner:
~/play/me/scripts/server local dev <project_name>
```

The backend runs on `PROJECT_PORT_BACKEND` (e.g., 8083 for TaskAI, 8080 for Pingrly).

### 5. Start the frontend with Vite proxy (CRITICAL)

**IMPORTANT: Use `VITE_PROXY_TARGET` with Vite's built-in proxy, NOT `VITE_API_URL`.**

Setting `VITE_API_URL` to a remote domain causes CORS errors because the browser sends cross-origin requests. Instead, Vite's dev server proxy handles `/api` requests server-side, forwarding them to the target — no CORS issues.

Projects with Vite have `vite.config.ts` configured to read `VITE_PROXY_TARGET`:

```typescript
// In vite.config.ts:
const proxyTarget = process.env.VITE_PROXY_TARGET || 'http://localhost:8080'
// ...
proxy: {
  '/api': { target: proxyTarget, changeOrigin: true, secure: true },
}
```

**If a project's vite.config.ts does NOT already read `VITE_PROXY_TARGET`**, add this pattern to it before starting.

Resolve the proxy target URL from the environment:

| Environment | VITE_PROXY_TARGET |
|-------------|-------------------|
| `local` | `http://localhost:<PROJECT_PORT_BACKEND>` (default, no env var needed) |
| `staging` | `https://staging.<PROJECT_DOMAIN>` |
| `uat` | `https://uat.<PROJECT_DOMAIN>` |
| `prod` | `https://<PROJECT_DOMAIN>` |

Then start:

```bash
cd <project_dir>/web
VITE_PROXY_TARGET=<url> npx vite --port <PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND> --host
```

The browser only talks to `localhost:<PORT>` — Vite proxies `/api/*` to the target server-side.

### 6. Report status

After starting, confirm all services are running:

```bash
# Check API (through proxy)
curl -s http://localhost:<PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND>/api/health

# Check frontend
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:<PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND>/
```

Print the URLs:
```
Local dev server running:
  Frontend: http://localhost:<PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND>
  API proxy: -> <VITE_PROXY_TARGET>
  Pointing to: <environment>
```

## Environment Domains by Project

These are read from `.me.sh`'s `PROJECT_DOMAIN`:

| Project | Domain | Staging | UAT |
|---------|--------|---------|-----|
| taskai | taskai.cc | staging.taskai.cc | uat.taskai.cc |
| pingrly | pingrly.com | staging.pingrly.com | uat.pingrly.com |
| blog | anshumanbiswas.com | staging.anshumanbiswas.com | - |
| folioworth | folioworth.com | staging.folioworth.com | uat.folioworth.com |
| elephanto | elephantoevents.ca | staging.elephantoevents.ca | - |
| flags | flagtgl.com | staging.flagtgl.com | - |

## Project Port Map

| Project | Backend | Frontend |
|---------|---------|----------|
| taskai | 8083 | 5174 |
| pingrly | 8080 | 3000 |
| blog | 22222 | - |
| folioworth | 8180 | 5173 |
| elephanto | 8080 | 3000 |
| flags | 8081 | 3000 |
| biswas | 9000 | 3001 |

## Important Notes

- **NEVER use `VITE_API_URL` to point to remote environments** — this causes CORS errors. Always use `VITE_PROXY_TARGET` with Vite's dev proxy instead.
- **Always start Docker postgres first** if the project uses PostgreSQL and pointing to `local`
- When pointing to prod/staging/uat, you don't need a local backend or database — the Vite proxy forwards API calls to the remote server
- OAuth login (GitHub/Google) works through the proxy since the browser sees everything as localhost
- Use `docker compose up -d postgres` (not `docker compose up`) to avoid starting ALL services
- The universal runner is at `~/play/me/scripts/server` — it discovers all projects with `.me.sh`

## Stopping

```bash
# Kill frontend dev server (find PID on the port)
lsof -ti:<PROJECT_PORT_FRONTEND> | xargs kill 2>/dev/null

# Kill backend (only if running locally)
lsof -ti:<PROJECT_PORT_BACKEND> | xargs kill 2>/dev/null

# Stop docker services
docker compose stop postgres
```

## Examples

**Start TaskAI locally pointing to production (most common):**
```bash
cd /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web
VITE_PROXY_TARGET=https://taskai.cc npx vite --port 5174 --host
# No backend or postgres needed — proxy handles everything
```

**Start TaskAI pointing to staging:**
```bash
cd /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web
VITE_PROXY_TARGET=https://staging.taskai.cc npx vite --port 5174 --host
```

**Start TaskAI fully local (with local backend + postgres):**
```bash
cd /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai
docker compose up -d postgres       # Start database
cd api && make dev &                 # Start backend on :8083
cd ../web && npx vite --port 5174 --host  # Frontend proxies to localhost:8080 by default
```

**Start Pingrly locally pointing to production:**
```bash
cd /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/pingrly/web  # or frontend/
VITE_PROXY_TARGET=https://pingrly.com npx vite --port 3000 --host
```

**Full Docker mode (all services containerized):**
```bash
./script/server local:start  # or docker compose up -d --build
```

content.text: The API is up on Postgres. Now I'll script the real scenario: four users, Elastio and Intelliviz teams, isolation checks, a member move, and a project invite and acceptance.

input.command:
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-anshumanbiswas-play-taskai/82ac5d09-8205-47a5-a238-caa15043da7e/scratchpad
cat > $S/scenario.sh <<'EOF'
set -u
API=http://localhost:8083
PG="docker exec -i taskai-teamtest-pg psql -U taskai -d taskai -tA"
j() { python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(eval(sys.argv[1]))" "$1"; }
signup() { # email first
  local code="code-$1"
  $PG -c "INSERT INTO invites (code, inviter_id) SELECT '$code', id FROM users LIMIT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  curl -s -XPOST $API/api/auth/signup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"email\":\"$1\",\"password\":\"Passw0rd!Passw0rd\",\"first_name\":\"$2\",\"last_name\":\"X\",\"invite_code\":\"$code\"}"
}
# first user needs an invite with an inviter; bootstrap via a system user row
$PG -c "INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash) VALUES ('seed@local.test','x') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING" >/dev/null
for u in "anshuman@local.test Anshuman" "bob@elastio.test Bob" "nakul@intelliviz.test Nakul" "faiz@intelliviz.test Faiz"; do set -- $u; signup $1 $2 > /tmp/.su.json; done
tok() { curl -s -XPOST $API/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"email\":\"$1\",\"password\":\"Passw0rd!Passw0rd\"}" | j "d['token']"; }
A=$(tok anshuman@local.test); B=$(tok bob@elastio.test); N=$(tok nakul@intelliviz.test); F=$(tok faiz@intelliviz.test)
c() { local t=$1; shift; curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$@"; }
echo "== A's teams"; c $A $API/api/teams
HOME_A=$(c $A $API/api/teams | j "d[0]['id']")
c $A -XPATCH $API/api/teams/$HOME_A -d '{"name":"Elastio"}' >/dev/null
IV=$(c $A -XPOST $API/api/teams -d '{"name":"Intelliviz"}' | j "d['id']")
echo "Elastio=$HOME_A Intelliviz=$IV"
# A adds bob to Elastio by exact email (search), nakul+faiz initially to Elastio too (the bug state)
for e in bob@elastio.test nakul@intelliviz.test faiz@intelliviz.test; do
  uid=$(c $A "$API/api/teams/$HOME_A/users/search?q=$e" | j "d[0]['id']"); c $A -XPOST $API/api/teams/$HOME_A/members -d "{\"user_id\":$uid}"; echo; done
echo "== Nakul's collaborators BEFORE split (bug: sees bob)"; c $N $API/api/me/collaborators; echo
echo "== Partial-name search from Nakul's own team for 'bob' BEFORE split (shares Elastio -> found)"; NT=$(c $N $API/api/teams | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([t['id'] for t in json.load(sys.stdin) if t['is_owner']][0])"); c $N "$API/api/teams/$NT/users/search?q=bob"; echo
# Split: move nakul & faiz from Elastio to Intelliviz
for e in nakul@intelliviz.test faiz@intelliviz.test; do
  mid=$(c $A $API/api/teams/$HOME_A/members | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([m['id'] for m in json.load(sys.stdin) if m['email']=='$e'][0])")
  c $A -XPOST $API/api/teams/$HOME_A/members/$mid/move -d "{\"target_team_id\":$IV}"; echo; done
echo "== Nakul's teams AFTER"; c $N $API/api/teams; echo
echo "== Nakul's collaborators AFTER (expect only anshuman+faiz under Intelliviz)"; c $N $API/api/me/collaborators; echo
echo "== Nakul reads Elastio roster (expect 404)"; c $N -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $API/api/teams/$HOME_A/members
echo "== Nakul legacy /team/members (his home team)"; c $N $API/api/team/members | j "[m['email'] for m in d]"
echo "== Nakul partial search 'bob' AFTER (expect [])"; c $N "$API/api/teams/$NT/users/search?q=bob"; echo
echo "== Nakul exact email search (expect bob)"; c $N "$API/api/teams/$NT/users/search?q=bob@elastio.test"; echo
echo "== Bob's collaborators (expect only anshuman)"; c $B $API/api/me/collaborators; echo
echo "== A creates project in Intelliviz, invites Faiz, Faiz accepts"
P=$(c $A -XPOST $API/api/projects -d "{\"name\":\"Intelliviz App\",\"team_id\":$IV}"); echo $P; PID=$(echo $P | j "d['id']")
FID=$(c $A $API/api/me/collaborators | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([m['user_id'] for m in json.load(sys.stdin) if m['email']=='faiz@intelliviz.test'][0])")
INV=$(c $A -XPOST $API/api/projects/$PID/invitations -d "{\"user_id\":$FID,\"role\":\"member\"}"); echo $INV
INVID=$(c $F $API/api/my/project-invitations | j "d[0]['id']"); c $F -XPOST $API/api/project-invitations/$INVID/accept; echo
echo "== Faiz can open project"; c $F -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $API/api/projects/$PID
echo "== Nakul (not invited) cannot"; c $N -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $API/api/projects/$PID
echo "== Nakul tries to create project in Elastio (expect 403)"; c $N -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -XPOST $API/api/projects -d "{\"name\":\"x\",\"team_id\":$HOME_A}"
echo "== A moves project to Elastio via PATCH"; c $A -XPATCH $API/api/projects/$PID -d "{\"team_id\":$HOME_A}" | j "(d['team_id'])"
echo "== Faiz leaves Intelliviz"; c $F -XPOST $API/api/teams/$IV/leave; echo
EOF
bash $S/scenario.sh 2>&1

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
entries.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

content.text:
Deploy TaskAI to all environments: staging → UAT → production.

## Usage
```
/deploy "feat: your commit message here"
```

If no message is provided as `feat(teams): separate teams so members only see their own team — skip UAT (staging → prod)`, use a generic message based on recent changes.

## Rules
- UAT is ALWAYS promoted from staging (main), never developed on directly
- Production is ALWAYS promoted from main after staging is verified
- Never manually SSH to servers — always use GitHub workflows

## Steps

### 1. Deploy to Staging
Run `./script/server deploy "feat(teams): separate teams so members only see their own team — skip UAT (staging → prod)"` (commits uncommitted changes, pushes to main, triggers GitHub Actions staging deploy).

If there are no uncommitted changes and `feat(teams): separate teams so members only see their own team — skip UAT (staging → prod)` is empty, just push: `git push origin main`.

### 2. Promote to UAT
```bash
./script/server promote staging uat
```

### 3. Promote to Production
```bash
./script/server promote staging prod
# or, if UAT was verified and you want to promote from UAT:
./script/server promote uat prod
```

You can chain steps 2 and 3:
```bash
./script/server promote staging uat && ./script/server promote staging prod
```

### 4. Report Status
Show a summary table:
| Environment | Action | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Staging | Deployed via push to main | https://staging.taskai.cc |
| UAT | Force-promoted from main | https://uat.taskai.cc |
| Production | GitHub Actions triggered | https://taskai.cc |

Monitor: https://github.com/anchoo2kewl/taskai/actions

input.command:
git add api/ && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(api): scope team visibility to the teams a user belongs to

Users working across companies (e.g. Elastio and Intelliviz) ended up in
one shared team, so everyone could see everyone. Teams are now managed
explicitly and members only ever see their own teams.

- Add /api/teams endpoints: list, create, rename, delete, members,
  add/invite, remove, move member between teams, sent invitations, leave
- Existing /api/team handlers resolve {teamId} and require membership;
  legacy routes act on a deterministic home team (oldest owned team)
- User search no longer exposes every registered user: partial matches
  only among people who already share a team, anyone else by exact email
- /me/collaborators returns team_id/team_name so pickers can group by team
- Projects expose team_id/team_name; create and PATCH accept team_id
  (caller must belong to the team; only the project owner can move it)
- Sent team invitations are visible to owners/admins only
- OpenAPI spec and table-driven tests for isolation, move, leave, delete
EOF
git add web/ && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(web): multi-team management in Settings and team-grouped project sharing

- New TeamsPanel: switch between teams, create a team, rename, delete,
  leave, add/invite people, and move members between teams
- Project Settings invite picker groups candidates by team, project's
  own team first; project owners can move a project to another team
- New-project modal lets multi-team users choose the team
- SearchSelect supports option groups
- Regenerated API types from the OpenAPI spec
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -2
